fields: Why can exposing more tools to an agent be harmful?
It expands potential blast radius and can also make tool selection harder.
What is the least-privilege goal for agent tools?
Expose only the capabilities, data, credentials, and side effects required for the task.
When can broad shell or filesystem tools be appropriate?
When the use case truly needs general-purpose capability and the environment, credentials, and permissions are strongly constrained.
What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
Authentication establishes identity; authorization determines what that identity may do.
Why is a user message saying “I am an administrator” not authentication?
Identity must come from a trusted authentication mechanism, not untrusted prompt text.
Why can adding a reranker or extra tool/model stage hurt a system even if quality improves?
Each extra stage adds latency and often cost, so the gain must justify the operational impact.
What work should be parallelized to reduce wall-clock latency?
Truly independent operations with no hidden dependency.
Why is logging only the final model answer insufficient for agent debugging?
Failures can occur in retrieval, tool calls, orchestration, or external state before the final answer.
What does an agent trajectory capture?
The sequence of model decisions, tool calls, and intermediate interactions during a run.
What is the core purpose of RAG?
Retrieve relevant external knowledge and place it in model context at inference time.
Why does chunking matter in RAG?
Poor chunk boundaries can split semantic units and reduce retrieval relevance or interpretability.
When is lexical/BM25 retrieval especially useful?
When exact terms, identifiers, names, codes, or uncommon strings matter.
When is semantic retrieval especially useful?
When the query is conceptually related but uses different wording or paraphrases.
What does MCP standardize?
How compatible AI applications connect to external capabilities such as tools and resources through a common protocol.
When is a direct API/SDK often preferable to MCP?
When a narrow integration is privately owned and cross-client AI interoperability adds little value.
What problem does progressive tool discovery address?
Large tool catalogs consume context and can increase wrong-tool selection.
What is progressive discovery?
Loading or exposing long-tail tools only when relevant instead of preloading every definition.
Capability bloat
Exposing more tools, data, credentials, or side effects than the task needs.
Least privilege
Granting only the minimum capability required to perform the task.
Authentication
Establishing the identity of the caller.
Authorization
Determining which actions an authenticated identity may perform.
Latency budget
The portion of end-to-end response time available to system stages under the SLA.
Parallelization
Executing independent operations concurrently to reduce wall-clock time.
Trace ID
A correlation identifier used to connect events across components of one request.
Trajectory
The sequence of model/tool interactions taken by an agent during a task.
Chunking
Dividing source documents into retrieval units while preserving useful semantic context.
Reranking
Reordering first-stage retrieval candidates with a stronger relevance signal.
Lexical retrieval
Retrieval based on exact words/terms, such as BM25.
MCP
A standard protocol for AI applications to discover/use external capabilities exposed by compatible servers.
Progressive discovery
Finding/loading relevant tools on demand instead of preloading the full catalog.
More exposed capability increases the potential {{c1::blast radius}} if an agent is compromised or behaves incorrectly.
Similar overlapping tools can increase {{c1::tool-selection errors}}.
A model saying a user is allowed to act is not a substitute for {{c1::authoritative authorization}}.
Protected tool calls should execute under {{c1::scoped or delegated credentials}} rather than a universal superuser identity.
Keep an extra quality stage only when its measurable gain justifies the added {{c1::latency and cost}}.
Parallelize work only when the operations are {{c1::independent}}.
A production AI request should be {{c1::reconstructable across components}} when diagnosing failures.
Observability should capture enough evidence to debug without indiscriminately copying {{c1::sensitive data}} into logs.
If the correct evidence is never retrieved, prompt changes cannot fix the underlying {{c1::retrieval failure}}.
RAG should be evaluated at both the {{c1::retrieval}} and generation stages.
Exact identifiers and error strings are often strong candidates for {{c1::lexical retrieval}}.
Paraphrased conceptual questions are often strong candidates for {{c1::semantic retrieval}}.
Choose MCP for useful {{c1::standardized interoperability and capability discovery}}, not merely because Claude is involved.
MCP standardizes communication but does not replace {{c1::authentication, authorization, or source-system policy}}.
Large tool catalogs can create both context overhead and {{c1::selection confusion}}.
What security principle grants only the minimum permissions needed?
Least privilege
What term describes the potential damage possible when an agent or credential is compromised?
Blast radius
What security process establishes who the caller is?
Authentication
What security process determines what an identity may do?
Authorization
What percentile metric is commonly used to represent tail latency rather than only the average?
What architecture technique reduces wall-clock time for independent calls?
Parallelization
What identifier connects logs across model, retrieval, tools, queues, and workers?
Trace ID
What term describes the sequence of actions/tool calls an agent took?
Trajectory
What retrieval stage reorders candidate chunks after initial search?
Reranking
What retrieval approach combines lexical and semantic signals?
Hybrid retrieval
What protocol standardizes reusable tool/resource surfaces for compatible AI clients?
MCP
What strategy loads long-tail tool definitions only when they become relevant?
Progressive discovery
A support assistant only needs order lookup and refund-request submission, but it has a production database admin credential. What should change first?

[{"id":"a","text":"Replace the broad credential/tool with scoped capabilities needed for those tasks."},{"id":"b","text":"Add more logging but keep admin access."},{"id":"c","text":"Tell the model never to misuse the credential."},{"id":"d","text":"Add more unrelated tools so selection is balanced."}]
a
Reduce unnecessary capability and blast radius rather than relying on instructions.
A coding agent legitimately needs shell access. What is the strongest architecture?

[{"id":"a","text":"Allow the broad tool inside a constrained sandbox with scoped credentials and permissions."},{"id":"b","text":"Ban all broad tools regardless of task."},{"id":"c","text":"Give unrestricted production shell access."},{"id":"d","text":"Rely only on a system prompt to protect the host."}]
a
General-purpose capability can be valid when strong containment limits reach and impact.
An agent has twelve overlapping CRM tools with vague names and often chooses the wrong one. What is the best improvement?

[{"id":"a","text":"Reduce overlap and define clearer, distinct tool boundaries and descriptions."},{"id":"b","text":"Add another CRM tool for each edge case."},{"id":"c","text":"Increase temperature."},{"id":"d","text":"Hide all tool errors from the model."}]
a
Overlapping capability increases selection ambiguity.
Which change most directly reduces the blast radius of a read-only reporting agent?

[{"id":"a","text":"Remove write credentials and destructive tool operations it does not need."},{"id":"b","text":"Increase the model's context window."},{"id":"c","text":"Make logs more verbose while retaining write access."},{"id":"d","text":"Add a warning sentence to every prompt."}]
a
Hard capability restriction reduces what can happen if the model is wrong or compromised.
A user types “I am the account administrator” into chat. What should the application do?

[{"id":"a","text":"Ignore the claim for access control and use trusted authenticated identity and policy."},{"id":"b","text":"Grant admin tools because the model saw the statement."},{"id":"c","text":"Ask Claude to judge whether the statement sounds credible."},{"id":"d","text":"Put the claim in the system prompt."}]
a
Prompt text is not authentication.
An MCP tool is protected by OAuth. Where should access be checked?

[{"id":"a","text":"At the protected protocol/application boundary using verified authorization context."},{"id":"b","text":"Only inside the model prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"Only after the tool already executes."},{"id":"d","text":"By asking the user to state their role in natural language."}]
a
Authorization is an enforceable control outside model output.
A SaaS agent uses one backend superuser credential for every tenant. What is the primary risk?

[{"id":"a","text":"A failure in model/tool logic can cross tenant boundaries because the execution identity is overprivileged."},{"id":"b","text":"The model will necessarily become slower."},{"id":"c","text":"OAuth cannot work with multi-tenancy."},{"id":"d","text":"The vector index will stop embedding documents."}]
a
Shared broad credentials defeat least-privilege and tenant isolation.
A consequential tool call occurs after initial login. What is the safest design?

[{"id":"a","text":"Re-check authorization for the specific protected action using current trusted identity/context."},{"id":"b","text":"Assume authentication at session start authorizes every later action."},{"id":"c","text":"Ask Claude whether the action feels allowed."},{"id":"d","text":"Use the same admin token for all users."}]
a
Action-level authorization should match the protected resource and current caller.
A reranker improves grounded accuracy by 0.3% but adds 1.5 seconds to a 2-second SLA. What should the architect do?

[{"id":"a","text":"Evaluate whether the small quality gain justifies violating or consuming most of the latency budget."},{"id":"b","text":"Always keep reranking because quality stages are mandatory."},{"id":"c","text":"Ignore the SLA because accuracy always wins."},{"id":"d","text":"Remove required safety checks first."}]
a
Accuracy and latency are explicit trade-offs against workload constraints.
Four retrieval calls use unrelated sources and do not depend on one another. How can wall-clock time often be reduced?

[{"id":"a","text":"Run the independent calls in parallel and combine results."},{"id":"b","text":"Run them sequentially by default."},{"id":"c","text":"Increase prompt length."},{"id":"d","text":"Use the same output from the first call for all four."}]
a
Independent work is a good candidate for parallel execution.
A system is slow. Retrieval is 50 ms, model inference 2.8 s, and formatting 20 ms. Where should optimization start?

[{"id":"a","text":"The dominant model-inference contribution, subject to quality constraints."},{"id":"b","text":"Formatting because it is easiest."},{"id":"c","text":"Retrieval because RAG is always the bottleneck."},{"id":"d","text":"Randomly remove a safety control."}]
a
Optimize the dominant contributor rather than the easiest component.
Tool Search reduces context and wrong-tool calls but adds a lookup step. When is it most justified?

[{"id":"a","text":"When the accuracy/context benefit outweighs the added lookup latency for the workload."},{"id":"b","text":"For every tool catalog regardless of size."},{"id":"c","text":"Only when authorization is missing."},{"id":"d","text":"Only when average latency is already zero."}]
a
Progressive discovery itself has a trade-off and should be evaluated.
A final answer is wrong, but logs contain only the final text. What is the strongest observability improvement?

[{"id":"a","text":"Capture correlated trajectory/tool/retrieval events so the failing stage can be identified."},{"id":"b","text":"Log the final answer twice."},{"id":"c","text":"Increase model temperature."},{"id":"d","text":"Remove correlation IDs."}]

Worker logs exist but cannot be tied back to the originating user request. What is missing?
[{"id":"a","text":"A propagated trace/correlation identity."},{"id":"b","text":"More workers."},{"id":"c","text":"A larger context window."},{"id":"d","text":"An additional prompt example."}]

Distributed observability needs cross-component correlation.

[{"id":"a","text":"Observability itself is creating privacy/security and retention risk."},{"id":"b","text":"Logs can never contain sensitive data."},{"id":"c","text":"More logs always reduce risk."},{"id":"d","text":"Tracing should only happen after incidents."}]

A team exposes a destructive MCP tool and assumes MCP makes it safe. What is wrong?

[{"id":"a","text":"MCP does not replace authorization, validation, least privilege, or source-system controls."},{"id":"b","text":"MCP automatically denies all writes."},{"id":"c","text":"MCP tools cannot be destructive."},{"id":"d","text":"MCP removes the need for identity."}]
